item.subject: science
item.stem:
Meera uses a concave shaving mirror to focus sunlight onto a dry scrap of newspaper in her courtyard. After a few moments, the paper begins to smoke at one small bright spot.
Why does the paper start to burn at that spot?

options.A: The mirror makes the sunlight warm as soon as the light touches the mirror's surface, and this heat passes to the paper.
options.B: The concave mirror reflects the parallel rays of sunlight so that they meet at one small point, concentrating the light energy there and raising the temperature enough to ignite the paper.
options.C: The mirror spreads the sunlight evenly over the paper, so the whole sheet warms up slowly until it catches fire.
options.D: The shiny surface of the mirror produces its own heat, which is transferred to the newspaper placed near it.
